First, some clarification: Sleep and Hibernation isn't the same thing. When a PC is Hibernating, it can only be turned on if you press the power button; while if it is Sleeping, it can be turned on more easily, like pressing a button on the keyboard.

 

Sleeping

To make the PC sleep via the command line is not possible without downloading a little tool. You'd think it would be possible with the command shutdown, but it can only hibernate the PC, not make it sleep. You will need a small program called psshutdown from Microsoft. The download contains a bunch of small programs but you only need psshutdown.exe.

By using the Task Scheduler we can make the PC sleep automatically.

Create a Task, set you triggers and set the program/script to the following but modified to YOUR location of psshutdown:

cmd.exe /c "C:\PATH\TO\FOLDER\psshutdown -d -t 0"

I'd recommend that under Conditions you select Start the task only if the computer is idle for and then 10min or something. This will prevent the PC from sleeping while you are using it.

 

Waking up

To make the PC wake up automatically, create a second task, and enter this in the program/script field:

cmd.exe /c "exit"

this will simply open a command prompt and then close it, making the PC wake up.

Under General select Run whether user is logged on of not, Run with highest privileges, and Configure for your OS, at the bottom.

Under Conditions select Wake the computer to run this task

Under Triggers set your desired triggers and it's done.
